title: On-call Scheduling Equity & Rotation Fairness
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This document defines Redwood's principles, operational rules, and concrete procedures for designing fair, equitable on-call rotations across engineering teams. It complements technical runbooks and incident playbooks by ensuring the human element (load distribution, swap mechanics, crediting, training cadence) is treated consistently and transparently.

Goals and principles:
- Psychological safety: avoid punitive scheduling, enable swaps without stigma, and protect time off.
- Predictability: publish rotations and expected load in advance so engineers can plan.
- Measurability: track on-call load and crediting with simple metrics that are reviewed monthly.
- Equity: distribute higher-impact shifts (nights, holidays, long-duration incidents) more evenly over time.
- Remediation: provide time and support after difficult incidents (post-incident rest and pairing).

Scope:
- Applies to all engineering teams with production on-call responsibilities (Serving Runtime, SRE, Platform, Private Deployments).
- Does not replace service-specific runbooks or incident escalation matrices; this document governs people/processes around schedules and fairness.

Key Definitions:
- Primary on-call: first responder for pager alerts and incident triage.
- Secondary on-call: backup for escalations after the primary acknowledges.
- Pager density: average number of P1/P2 alerts per 7-day period for a rotation slot (tracked per service).
- On-call credit: a points system used to quantify burden for each shift (see table below).

Rotation design rules (hard constraints):
1) Shift length and cadence:
   - Default shift: 1 week for Primary (Monday 00:00 UTC through Sunday 23:59 UTC).
   - Night-only rotations (where applicable): 7 nights, 00:00–08:00 local shift.
   - Max consecutive shifts: 2 consecutive primary weeks unless opt-in approved by manager.

2) Maximum weekly on-call load:
   - No engineer should exceed 25% of total primary weeks in a rolling 12-month window unless explicitly opted-in.
   - When a team has fewer than 6 eligible engineers, People Ops will initiate a backfill discussion with managers.

3) Swap and carry rules:
   - Swaps are permitted with 48-hour minimum notice for primary week swaps; emergency swaps allowed by manager or rotation owner.
   - Carryover compensation: if a swap results in an engineer taking >50% of a particularly noisy week after swap, the original owner receives 1.0 on-call credit and the swap-taker receives 1.5 credits (see credits table).

On-call crediting system (purpose: objective fairness accounting)
| Shift type | Base credit | Incident multiplier | Example note |
|-----------|-------------|---------------------|--------------|
| Standard week (primary) | 1.0 | 1.0 | baseline |
| Night week (primary) | 1.25 | 1.0 | nights counted higher |
| Holiday week (company-declared) | 1.5 | 1.0 | US major holidays |
| Week with >3 P1s | 1.0 | 1.5 | multiplier applied post-week |
| Major incident (SEV1 lasting >4h) | additional 1.0 | n/a | added to credits for that engineer

Operational table (quick reference):
| Rule | Value | Owner / Notes |
|------|-------|--------------|
| Default primary shift | 1 week | People Ops & Team Leads |
| Max consecutive primary weeks | 2 | People Ops | Opt-in allowed |
| Swap notice (standard) | 48 hours | Engineers | Use /oncall swap-requests channel |
| Emergency swap path | Manager or Rotation Owner approval | People Ops handles exceptions |
| Post-incident rest window | 24–72 hours | Manager + SRE Lead | For SEV1 responders

Procedures (step-by-step):
1) Rotation creation (rotation owner responsibility):
   a) Define eligible roster and publish 90-day calendar.
   b) Annotate expected pager density for that service (low/medium/high).
   c) Set blackout dates where applicable (major conferences, CTO vacation windows).

2) Swap workflow (engineer-initiated):
   1. Create a swap request using the On-call Bot: /oncall swap @alice for week 2025-06-08
   2. Confirm acceptance by both parties in Slack within 48 hours.
   3. Update the rotation tool (rota.redwood.internal) and notify rotation-owner channel.
   4. The swap triggers automated credit adjustments in People Ops ledger.

3) Emergency swap (manager/owner):
   - Manager opens a ticket to People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com) and pings rotation-owner. People Ops logs the exception and adjusts credits accordingly.

4) Post-incident relief & pairing:
   - For any SEV1 where an engineer had >2 hours of continuous triage, the manager must schedule one day of focused coding-free pairing or rest in the following 7 days. Pairing can include knowledge transfer for runbook improvements.

Fairness mechanisms and automated checks:
- Monthly fairness job (run by People Ops) computes: per-engineer rolling 12-month credit totals, average pager density per slot, and outlier detection (top and bottom 5%).
- Escalation: If an engineer is in the top 5% of credits, rotation-owner and manager schedule a remediation meeting within 7 days to rebalance future rotations.
- Opt-in and opt-out: engineers can opt-in for above-average on-call loads for compensation (extra PTO day or monetary stipend); opt-out requires manager sign-off and must not leave team below minimum coverage.

Metrics and reporting (what we track):
- Credits per engineer (rolling 12 months) — target mean and variance by team.
- Pager density by rotation slot (P1/P2s per week).
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to mitigate (MTTM) while on primary on-call.
- Incidents per shift and cumulative incident duration.
- Post-incident rest usage rate (percentage of SEV1s that received scheduled rest).

Game day & training cadence (to reduce inequitable burden):
- Frequency: quarterly team game days focused on high-burden services.
- Scope: simulated P1s that exercise the entire runloop (pager, bridge, rollback).
- Participation: every engineer must participate in at least one team game day per 12 months; People Ops and team leads ensure equitable assignments.
- Debrief: each game day produces a 1-page debrief with remediation items and impact on credits if game day uncovered chronic load imbalance.

Customer communications and scheduling conflicts:
- For planned maintenance that intersects multiple on-call shifts, rotation owners must notify affected engineers 14 days in advance and publish a customer-facing status page schedule draft 7 days prior.
- If maintenance falls on a holiday week (1.5 credit), rotate ownership to minimize repeated holiday burden for the same engineer across a 12-month window.

Examples (templates):
- Swap request (Slack):
  "Hey @oncall-bot, I need to swap my primary week 2025-06-08. Willing to take 2025-07-06 in exchange. @bob please confirm."

- Manager escalation email (People Ops):
  Subject: Emergency on-call swap request for team Runtime – week 2025-06-08
  Body: "Manager: Priya Nair. Reason: family emergency. Affected engineer: @alice. Request: swap to @bob. Please approve and adjust credits."

- Post-incident rest note (for DEBRIEF):
  "SEV1 on 2025-02-21 — primary responder @charles had 6 hours of continuous triage; scheduled 1 day of rest on 2025-02-25 and paired knowledge transfer on 2025-02-26."

Enforcement and exceptions:
- People Ops performs quarterly audits. Repeated non-compliance (e.g., consistently exceeding max consecutive shifts without opt-in) will be raised to the manager and Engineering leadership.
- Exceptions for small teams (<6 eligible engineers) are permitted with a mandatory remediation plan to grow the eligible roster or hire backfill.

Implementation notes (tools & automation):
- Rota tool: rota.redwood.internal (API available at https://rota.redwood.internal/api/v1). Example: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROTATOKEN" https://rota.redwood.internal/api/v1/rotations/team-runtime
- On-call Bot Slack commands: /oncall swap, /oncall schedule, /oncall credits @me
- Fairness job: runs on the 1st of each month and writes to People Ops ledger (spreadsheet + internal database).

Ownership and escalation matrix for this policy:
- Policy owner: People Ops (Maya Chen).
- Execution owner: Rotation owners (team SRE leads).
- Review cadence: Annual policy review (People Ops + Eng SRE + Legal for compliance impacts).

Appendix A: Example credit ledger CSV format (header row)
- engineer_email,team,week_start,week_end,shift_type,base_credit,incident_credit,total_credit,notes

Appendix B: Frequently asked questions (short)
Q: Can I sell my on-call shift?
A: No. Selling shifts for money outside company opt-in programs is prohibited. All swaps must be tracked in the rota tool.

Q: What counts as a holiday week?
A: Company-declared holidays (see HR calendar). Local public holidays that are not company-declared are treated as standard weeks unless the team agrees otherwise.

Q: How are credits converted to compensation?
A: Credits are primarily used for internal fairness tracking. Opt-in compensation programs (extra PTO or stipend) are handled by People Ops and require manager approval.
